items.title: Eddie B. Edwards Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: And then Spivaro came with us when we went to the Casino Gardens.

ctx.x: I wondered if you could tell me when the drums changed there. After the Schiller Cafe.

After the Schiller. Three months in 1916, Stein was with us. He stayed on and got another band, and for I think three weeks at the Del Abbey, we had a drummer, a Chicago boy. I don't remember his name now. And then Spivaro came with us when we went to the Casino Gardens.
And your clarinet changed too, didn't it? Somewhere around there.

items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: In a short while, Edwards started writing to me. For this reason, I had been playing with Giordina, with Edwards.

ctx.x: And all the white people that really opened their door and enjoyed themselves, paid a little amount, whatever it was. It wasn't much money. You know, people can't just... But there was never no dissension. No. Never none of that stuff. That's the ridiculous thing, that dissension for... My gosh, I can never... Well, take for instance, those boys just go out there and catch catfish. Catfish is the big type of fish that is the best fried fish. In fact, I still think catfish... You ought to know, because you're one…

play the bass with you, I'll go buy one on time. I said okay I'll take you over to the World Line Music Store and I did. We got a big sousaphone for him and he brought it down to his job. He had it in traction high, he had it hung up so that all he had to do was get into this big part of it. A bell. And he'd stand up and play. And he played with him. And he was a member of that little band of mine for many, for the entire length of time at the La Vida, which from there his reputation became known and they became…
Henry. I want to get that straight. There's so many out.

items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: I used to play with Ernest. I was playing with Ernest. He was playing with Ernest. He was playing trumpet and Edwards was playing trombone and back there was playing clarinet.

ctx.x: But it's in French. It doesn't say that. Oh, I know him. I don't think it says that. I can't read French myself. Oh, it's in French, the book? Yeah, but it tells about, you're talking about Ernest Jodtonio and Tony Jodtonio both.

Well, Tony Jodtonio played with Emile's brother. I used to play with Ernest. I was playing with Ernest. He was playing with Ernest. He was playing trumpet and Edwards was playing trombone and back there was playing clarinet.
Well, let's start at the very beginning of your life. Where were you born? I was born right here in New Orleans. Exactly. Do you remember that address? No. Street?
